primary_source.paper: Stechly, Valmeekam & Kambhampati, "Chain of Thoughtlessness? An Analysis of CoT in Planning"

trace_source: tasks/blocksworld/published_trace.txt, verbatim copy of vendor/cot-planning/example_query_prompts/blocksworld_state_tracking/upb.txt (the 'Blocksworld Universal Algorithm' n-shot CoT prompt exemplar shipped in the paper's own repo; commit recorded in vendor/cot-planning.commit)
format_description: Each step is a numbered block: '<n>. Current State: <comma-joined list of clear/on-table/holding/on predicates in prose>' then a line 'Action: <pick up|put down|stack|unstack> the Block <X> [from on top of / on top of the Block <Y>]', then 'Reason: <prose precondition justification>', then 'Resulting State: <comma-joined predicate list, same prose style>'.
theory_citation: Applying a given, fully-specified action to a known blocksworld state is a constant-size predicate update (no search) -- TC0-class simulation. Planning (finding the action sequence) is the hard direction; see Gupta & Nau 1992 'On the complexity of blocks-world planning' (blocksworld optimal planning is NP-hard) and Slaney & Thiebaux 2001 'Blocks World revisited' (polynomial planning algorithms exist for the standard 4-operator variant used here) -- not applicable to the tracking-only formulation this desk entry scores.

knob.name: blocks (number of blocks in the domain)
knob.granularity: integer, paper sweeps 3-20 (Figure 2); depth (plan length in actions) is a secondary knob, not separately scored here

published_data.metric: accuracy on table-to-stack Blocksworld across CoT prompt specificity, 261 instances
published_data.values: zero-shot: 19.1% / 9.96% / 3.83%. zero-shot CoT: 21% / 10.34% / 4.98%. domain-specific n-shot + Progression Proof CoT: 15.3% / 4.59% / 6.89%. domain-specific n-shot + Blocksworld Universal Algorithm CoT: 37.1% / 37.1% / 51.3%. problem-class-specific n-shot + Stacking Prompt: 40.6% / 24.5% / 59.3%.

published_data.metric: accuracy vs number of blocks (3-20), all 7 prompt types, on each model's intended problem distribution
published_data.values: all curves fall from roughly 60-100% at 3 blocks to under 20-30% by 8-10 blocks regardless of CoT specificity, except the narrowest 'Stacking Prompt' which stays higher longer; exact per-block-count values are read off a line chart, not tabulated, so only the qualitative decay shape is asserted here.

published_data.paper: karthikv792/cot-planning repo, results/blocksworld_state_tracking/*.json (data released alongside arXiv:2405.04776, recomputed directly from the vendored result files, not from paper text)
published_data.metric: plan-generation accuracy on the blocksworld_state_tracking domain (planning variant, model produces the action sequence), 270 instances per run
published_data.values: claude-3-opus CoT (upb prompt): 3/270 = 1.1%. claude-3-opus no-CoT (po prompt): 31/270 = 11.5%. gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 CoT: 9/270 = 3.3%. gpt-4_chat CoT: 12/270 = 4.4%. gpt-4_chat no-CoT: 20/270 = 7.4%.

notes: published_trace.txt contains two concatenated worked examples from the same file (6 steps then 12 steps = 18 steps total); tokens_per_step = tokens_total / 18. state_bits uses the count of distinct n-block blocksworld configurations at n=4 (the trace's own block count: A,B,C,D). CORRECTED 2026-09-16 during implementation: an earlier revision of this file used OEIS A000522 (floor(e*n!), 'arrangements of up to n items') -> 65 -> 6.0 bits, which is the wrong sequence. A blocksworld configuration is an unordered SET of ordered stacks, i.e. a 'set of lists', OEIS A000262 (1, 1, 3, 13, 73, 501, 4051), so n=4 gives 73 hand-empty configurations; adding the states with a block in hand (4 choices of held block x A000262(3) = 4 x 13 = 52) gives 125 reachable states, log2(125) ~= 6.97 bits. Verified by exhaustive BFS over the 4-operator domain in tasks/blocksworld/task.py. The hand is included because the tracked state in the published trace includes it ('the hand is currently holding Block C'). This is the published trace's own state-space size, not a general formula fit to an arbitrary blocks knob. gemma-2-2b and Meta-Llama-3-8B tokenizer.json are gated on Hugging Face and no HF token was available in this environment; tokenized instead via the ungated mirrors unsloth/gemma-2-2b and NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3-8B (community re-uploads of the same official weights/tokenizer, not retrained). Qwen/Qwen2-7B tokenizer.json fetched directly from the official (ungated) repo. This desk.json scores the tracking-style reading of the trace (state after each given action) even though the vendored trace and the accuracy numbers above are for the PLANNING formulation (model produces the actions, not just tracks given ones) -- per AMENDMENT 2 the metrics describe the task as published/as the source repo's own format, and that format is planning; theory_class/local_redundancy/state_bits/etc. are scored for what tracking through this published trace's state representation would look like, since that is what those fields ask about.
